title: FSM state (pipeline current-state file)
description: fsm-state.json at run root. Durable current state of the pipeline FSM (see references/state-machine.md). Models the phase, the executor<->verifier loop substate (Q = EXECUTE|VERIFY|ADJUDICATE|RETRY|ESCALATE|DONE), the bounded retries counter (max 2), gate flags, and per-unit status. The single top-level `loop` object tracks the MOST RECENTLY TRANSITIONED unit; because units run in parallel waves, each `units[]` item MAY additionally carry its own durable per-unit `retries` + `loop_state` (D-02/IMP-11). Loop cross-check iteration<=retries+1 is enforced in validate_run.py for both the `loop` slot and every `units[]` item that records `retries`.

model.description: Optional: the model this run executed under (recorded so model-scoped learnings can bind). Absent => unrecorded.

validator_version.description: OPTIONAL (F1/WP-E). The plugin/validator version this run is currently held to: init_run.sh stamps it from .claude-plugin/plugin.json when it scaffolds the run, and REFRESHES it to the current plugin version on every phase advance (init_run.sh --restamp, raise-only ratchet — U08). On a live run it therefore names the version current at the LATEST phase advance, not the version that scaffolded the run. Enables the version-skew policy (state-machine.md §5): the CURRENT validator's findings on a run stamped with an OLDER version are expected-skew, not defects. Gates no FSM transition, but DOES arm the version-gated new-run presence requirements that validate_run.py instruments with `_skew_record` — deliberately NOT enumerated here, because a hand-maintained list rots: the N-I45 version-skew NOTE prints the live set of arms a given run's stamp suppressed, and spec_check's SC8 fails if any `_i27_semver_ge` arm is ever added without its recorder. See state-machine.md §5 (AF-41). An absent stamp (legacy/pre-1.7.0 runs) is judged exactly as before: None => False on every semver comparison, so those arms stay silent and no unstamped archived run is newly penalized.

accepted_incomplete.description: OPTIONAL, ADDITIVE (I44 / predicate-spec.md §2.3). The recorded per-unit sign-off override: a human decision to sign off knowingly while the named units' verification is still open. DELIBERATELY UNCONSTRAINED here — any JSON value is schema-valid — so that a MALFORMED override reaches validate_run.py's fail-closed arm `I44 sign-off closure (accepted_incomplete malformed)` instead of being intercepted by the schema layer (the predicate, not the schema, is what must fail closed). Well-formed shape: {units:[<unit id>,...], rationale:<non-blank str>, decision_ref:<str containing 'DECISIONS.md'>, accepted_at?:str, accepted_by?:str}; units/rationale/decision_ref are read by the predicate, accepted_at/accepted_by never are. DECLARED so the top-level additionalProperties:false is not violated (the lens2 rule); NEVER required, so no archived fsm-state.json becomes invalid.

anchors_baseline_hash.description: OPTIONAL (1.10.0; schema-deltas §D). Ledger-side mirror of dialogues.json.anchors_baseline.content_hash. As of 1.10.1 it is CROSS-CHECKED by I39-7 when present: a present mirror MUST equal that content_hash (Limitation X hardening — a coordinated rewrite must then also rewrite fsm-state, raising the cost to three files; adoption-gated on presence, absent => silent). Absent => valid (the zero-delta primary posture; round counters + the anchor baseline live in dialogues.json, DP-21). DECLARED so the top-level additionalProperties:false is not violated (the lens2 rule); NEVER required (archive-safe) and NEVER gates a transition — still PRESERVES (GV-28).

accepted_prose.description: OPTIONAL, ADDITIVE (I50-3, 1.14.0). The recorded per-file override for the plain-language prose bounds: a decision to ship a named ledger file knowingly over one of the three bounds. DELIBERATELY UNCONSTRAINED here — any JSON value is schema-valid — so a MALFORMED override reaches validate_run.py's fail-closed arm instead of being intercepted by the schema layer, exactly as accepted_incomplete does. Well-formed shape: {files:[<run-relative filename>,...], rationale:<non-blank str>, decision_ref:<str containing 'DECISIONS.md'>}. A named file is DOWNGRADED from FAIL to a greppable N-I50 NOTE — never suppressed, never covering a file it does not name, and fails closed if malformed. NOT in the source recommendation: added by the implementing run because I50-3 is a HARD FAIL on prose style with no other recorded way out, and this repository's own idiom for 'available but loud' is accepted_incomplete. Disclosed rather than smuggled.
accepted_prose.$comment: Intentionally schema-unconstrained; see the accepted_incomplete precedent above.

blast_accepted.description: OPTIONAL, ADDITIVE, VALIDATOR-OWNED (I64, 1.15.0 blast radius). The recorded per-item blast-radius override: a human decision to sign off knowingly while NAMED blast-radius findings stay open. It is the ONLY sanctioned way past a blast FAIL on a gated run, and it is per item, never a switch: it can only DOWNGRADE each finding it names from FAIL to a greppable NOTE — it never suppresses a finding, never covers an item it does not name, and never turns a blast check off. Well-formed shape: {items:[<named finding>,...], rationale:<non-blank str>, decision_ref:<str containing 'DECISIONS.md'>}; that shape is owned and checked by validate_run.py, which fails closed on a malformed value. DELIBERATELY UNCONSTRAINED here — any JSON value is schema-valid — so a MALFORMED override reaches the validator's fail-closed arm instead of being intercepted by the schema layer, exactly as accepted_incomplete does. DECLARED so the top-level additionalProperties:false is not violated; NEVER required, so no archived fsm-state.json becomes invalid.
blast_accepted.$comment: Intentionally schema-unconstrained; see the accepted_incomplete precedent above.

run_mode.description: I51 (1.14.0, Ask 3) — the run's autonomy mode, chosen at a Phase-0/1 dialogue with NO ASSUMED DEFAULT. 'manual' is today's behaviour (zero machine-closed gates). 'critical-only' machine-closes non-critical gates and HALTS for the human on a critical one. 'automatic' machine-closes every gate including sign-off, with analyst dissent recorded rather than escalated. This is a NEW TOP-LEVEL PROPERTY on a closed object, so it is a genuine schema edit — added to `properties` only, NEVER to `required`, so every archived run directory keeps validating. I51-1's presence requirement is VERSION-GATED on validator_version >= 1.14.0 for the same reason: written unarmed it would red every archived run in .wip/ on the next validator run.

context_contract.description: I52/I59 (1.14.0, Ask 4) — the orchestrator's turn contract, promoting the run directory from failure-path fallback to declared working memory: 'You hold no history between obligations. Before discharging any obligation, name the run-directory file you will read to discharge it, and read it.' Absent => the mechanism is not adopted and both predicates are silent (archive-safe). HONEST BOUNDARY: this makes statelessness LEGIBLE, never TRUE — no predicate can establish that the orchestrator READ the named file rather than answering from residual context, which is why the enforcement class is OBSERVABLE and ENFORCED is explicitly disclaimed.

projection_ceiling_bytes.description: Ceiling on units/<Uxx>/adjudication.json. 12000 is an ASSUMED design parameter (~4.6% of the measured 262,448 B debrief+verify pair), not a measurement — tune it on first use. NOTE: the source recommendation's claimed net saving of ~101,808 tokens/unit is WITHDRAWN as unreachable at this ceiling; adopt the mechanism for the context relief, not for the saving.

progress_clock.description: I54 (1.14.0, Drift fix 2) — the deliverable clock. Counts units ADJUDICATED since the last graph.json unit marked deliverable:'ships' reached PASS. Deliberately NOT wall-clock (the run has no trustworthy clock source other than an agent typing one — L3 records ledger timestamps drifting ~7h from unforgeable sources) and NOT tokens (both per-unit token figures on disk are declarations by the agent being measured). It is a count the validator RECOMPUTES, which is what makes it evidence rather than narration. Absent => mechanism not adopted (I54 silent — archive-safe), the same posture `depth` uses.

last_ship_unit.description: Unit id of the most recent deliverable:'ships' unit that reached PASS, or null if none has.

surface_threshold.description: Default 3. DERIVED, not chosen by taste: the incident report records the failure at four ('My run hit four in a row'), so three fires strictly before the observed failure and after two — the smallest count that is not simply 'two in a row', a shape any dependency chain produces. Anyone with more than one incident should re-derive it.

surfaced_at.description: APPEND-ONLY. One record per surfacing event. 'Surfaced unprompted' cannot mean the run interrupts you — SKILL.md forbids ending a turn outside a gate — so it means three writes at the next boundary the run reaches anyway: a PROGRESS.md line, a record here, and a mandatory line in the run's next reply whatever that reply is for. In fully-automatic mode the audience is 'machine' and the breach lands in the run's final summary; it is NEVER silently dropped. A clock breach is explicitly NOT critical and never interrupts in critical-only mode: a threshold crossing is a DISCLOSURE, not a choice, and the choice it might prompt belongs to I56.

audience.description: COLLISION 8 — a machine-AUDIENCE disclosure is NOT a machine-DECISION. These records must stay DISJOINT from machine-decisions.json: I51 quantifies over decisions only, and if these surfacings landed in that channel the count of machine-made decisions (the one number a human reviewing an unattended run actually needs) would become uninterpretable.

wall_clock_advisory.description: OPTIONAL colour, script-stamped from `date` in the same command that writes the line — never typed from memory. Read by no predicate, and the trigger for nothing.

signoff_confirmed.description: The human accepted the deliverable at the Phase-8 sign-off gate (G-signoff / T12). REQUIRED true to reach phase DONE — validate_run.py's REQUIRED_GATES lists it for DONE, so a run at DONE without it is INVALID (D-06). Like personas_confirmed, the flag is a human attestation the validator checks the PRESENCE of, not the genuineness of. Its meaning is UNCHANGED by 1.14.0's I51: only a human sets it, and setting it without a human remains a defect. A machine-closed gate sets the DISJOINT sibling key below, never this one.

personas_machine_closed.description: I51 (1.14.0). The DISJOINT machine channel. Set true iff the Phase-1 gate was closed by the main agent under a recorded run_mode having consulted an independent analyst, with a backing machine-decisions.json record. I51-2 makes it a FAIL to set this AND personas_confirmed on the same gate. This key lives inside the OPEN `gates` object, so it costs no schema edit; it is declared here for documentation only.

clarification_machine_closed.description: I51 (1.14.0). As personas_machine_closed, for the Phase-2 clarification gate.

signoff_machine_closed.description: I51 (1.14.0). As personas_machine_closed, for the Phase-8 sign-off gate. This is the key that lets an honest fully-automatic run reach DONE: REQUIRED_GATES is widened to `<g>_confirmed OR <g>_machine_closed`, so a run no longer has to choose between SKILL.md's 'setting it without a human is a defect' and finishing.

starvation_cap_n.description: I56 (1.14.0, Drift fix 4). Default 3. CHOSEN, NOT MEASURED, and the section says so: the single datum supports FOUR and says nothing about three, so 3 is a judgement calibrated to fire before the incident's fourth investigation and after two. Raise it to tune. Lives in the open `gates` object at zero schema cost.

starvation_cap_enabled.description: I56 (1.14.0). Default true. Set false to disable the cap — which converts I56 from a FAIL into a greppable NOTE recording that the cap was off and what each run(d) reached. Switching a gate off must not erase the evidence it would have produced, so complete silence here would make the disabling unauditable.

loop.description: Executor<->verifier loop substate for the MOST RECENTLY TRANSITIONED unit in Phase 6. With parallel waves >1 unit may be in-flight; this single slot is a back-compat snapshot of the last unit to transition, while each unit's durable per-unit loop state lives in its `units[]` item (`retries` + `loop_state`) — D-02/IMP-11. retries is HARD-BOUNDED at 2 (termination invariant; variant V=2-retries). state uses the loop's Q vocabulary.

items.description: Per-unit durable record. `retries` + `loop_state` are OPTIONAL (D-02/IMP-11): they make each in-flight unit's correction-loop substate representable during parallel waves, instead of only the single top-level `loop` slot. When `retries` is present, validate_run.py cross-checks the unit's verify.iteration <= retries+1 (I4, same bound as the loop slot).

projection_bytes.description: I52 (1.14.0, Ask 4). OPTIONAL. The recorded size of units/<unit_id>/adjudication.json — the bounded projection the orchestrator reads INSTEAD of the whole debrief+verify pair. A CLAIM: I52 recomputes it from the file on disk and FAILs on disagreement, so it can never be narration.

expansion.description: OPTIONAL (Bounded Graph Amendments). The Phase-6 graph-amendment fuel budget. Seeded at Phase 4 (default min(N0,8); a non-default value comes only from an explicit instruction at an earlier gate — decomposition has no human touchpoint, U2/D-C: exactly three human gates). 0 or absent => BGA disabled (today's behavior). fuel is monotone-decreasing: only an amendment writes it, mirroring the retries counter. validate_run.py I18 cross-checks fuel_remaining == fuel_initial - sum(amendment fuel_cost) and fuel_remaining >= 0. Top-level is additionalProperties:false, so this property must be declared.

depth.description: OPTIONAL (depth tiers). Human-gated run depth tier, confirmed at the Phase-1 persona gate (rides the existing gate — no new gate flag; REQUIRED_GATES untouched). tier = EFFECTIVE tier; confirmed_tier/proposed_tier are the immutable gate record; skipped_floors is the canonical DT-K<n>@<confirmed_tier> delta disclosure ([] only for full), re-rendered for the CONFIRMED tier on divergent confirmation; phase2_touch records the unconditional Phase-2 keep-or-raise touch; overrides[] is append-only and UPWARD-only (light<standard<full) with a DECISIONS.md ref + pending_units snapshot per entry — the orchestrator can never lower a confirmed tier, and raised floors bind only units not yet PASS-verified (per-unit tier_at_verification in verify). Absent => mechanism not adopted (validator I28 silent — archive-safe). Top-level is additionalProperties:false, so this property must be declared.

blast.description: OPTIONAL (1.15.0 blast radius). The run's blast-radius baseline, written once by init_run.sh when it scaffolds the run. `mode` is how file footprints are captured for this run: 'git' (content-addressed tree ids of the workspace minus the run directory and .wip/), 'snapshot' (no git: per-file sha256 entries plus a content store under the run directory), 'none' (no capture mechanism). `base_sha` is the HEAD commit at scaffold time (40-hex; null without git or without a first commit). `base_tree_digest` is 'sha256:<64-hex>' over the workspace CONTENT at scaffold time (git: sha256 of 'tree:<tree id>\n'; snapshot: sha256 over the sorted '<path>\t<sha256>\n' lines), or null. `workspace_root` is the absolute, realpath'd workspace the captures read. `dirty_at_start[]` lists the paths the workspace already showed as modified or untracked at scaffold time — pre-existing state, not the run's work. `tool_version` names the writer. Absent => mechanism not adopted (archive-safe); whether a run of a given stamp MUST carry it is decided by the version-gated validator predicates, never by `required` here. Carries no key that switches a blast check off; the only override is the per-item top-level `blast_accepted`.
